title: Figure and Ground
subtitle: One tiling of birds and fish, read two ways
technique: Figure–ground reversal: a two-creature tiling over a vertical tonal gradient, where whichever creature matches the ground's tone stops being a shape and the other becomes the figure
refs: M. C. Escher, Sky and Water I, 1938
M. C. Escher, Day and Night, 1938
blurb: Light birds and dark fish share one tiling; above the band the birds are figures and fly off, below it the fish are, and they swim away.
